item.title: Hofmeister‐Type Anion Regulation Suppresses Electrochemical Acidification for Long‐Life TEMPO‐Based Aqueous Flow Batteries
item.description:
تنظیم آنیونی هافمایستر با جایگزینی کلرید با سولفات، اسیدی شدن الکتروشیمیایی را سرکوب و عمر باتری جریان آبی TEMPO را افزایش میدهد.
Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This study reveals that TEMPO catholyte acidification proceeds via chloride oxidation and reversible proton release, independent of substituents. It identifies Hofmeister-type anion regulation as the key control, showing kosmotropic sulfate suppresses acidification versus chaotropic chloride. This enables 97.6% capacity retention over 300 cycles and broad lifetime gains, establishing electrolyte engineering for durable aqueous flow batteries.
🏷 aqueous flow battery · TEMPO · Hofmeister anion · acidification · cycling stability

item.description:

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Inspired by lotus-leaf hierarchies, this work grows bifunctional MOF crystals in situ on cellulose acetate, combining micro-sized mechanical support with nano-sized polar sites for Li⁺ transport. The resulting solid electrolyte achieves 2.9×10⁻³ S cm⁻¹ conductivity, 0.61 transference number, 5.5 V stability, and 80.9% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 4.6 V, offering a practical route to upgrade commercial membranes.
